findings.detail: scored 0 — The answer is a bare refusal that withholds the requested table values and comparison making none of the rubric's must-contain points though it violates no must-not item. Unmet: gives the USGS table value at 20.0 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.09 mg/L; gives the EPA chart value at 20 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.06 mg/L; States the difference is 0.03 mg/L and assesses its significance against the applicable procedure not as universally insignificant; notes the USGS values are generated from the Benson and Krause equations; Compares the 0.03 mg/L difference with the USGS saturation-check tolerance of ±0.2 mg/L; advises using the table belonging to whichever protocol the work is being done under consistently rather than mixing them

scored 0 — The answer makes the annual-verification and NIST-traceable-reference points but violates a must-not by telling the user to 'adjust or replace the sensor' to match the reference and it omits the ±0.2 C accuracy figure and the calibration-solution/evaporation point. Unmet: Gives required accuracy as about ±0.2 C where the sensor is bundled on a multiparameter instrument and used to correct another parameter; States calibration solution must cover probe and temperature sensor; identifies evaporation of moisture as a DO air-calibration concern

scored 0 — The answer gives the two table solubilities but computes a 1.05 mg/L drop (not 0.99) omits any barometric-pressure dependence omits the brackish salinity correction and presents a definite residual drop rather than saying it cannot be established — and by applying freshwater solubility values unchanged to the brackish site it violates a must-not item. Unmet: States freshwater equilibrium solubility at 760 mmHg falls by 0.99 mg/L from 15 C to 20 C as a conditional benchmark not a ceiling on measured DO; States equilibrium saturation also depends on barometric pressure so the site's actual pressure changes the benchmark; States that in brackish water the freshwater value must be reduced by a salinity correction factor before comparison; States the actual warming contribution and remaining site-specific drop cannot be established from these readings alone (pressure salinity initial saturation not given); conditional estimate labelled with assumptions acceptable

scored 0 — The answer claims the EPA 180.1 column has the same precision as the USGS column in every range and gives 1 NTU for the 40–<100 range under EPA which is an invented EPA resolution and asserts identical resolutions across ranges violating two must-not items. Unmet: States EPA Method 180.1 reports 63.7 as 65 to the nearest 5 units in the 40 to under 100 range

scored 0 — The answer asserts the probe's raw ORP millivolts are the same as Eh ('the only difference is the terminology') violating the must-not against treating them as interchangeable and it omits the reference-electrode correction points. Unmet: states that Eh is an equilibrium potential developed at the boundary between a noble-metal electrode and the water and reflects the redox-active species in solution; states that the millivolts the probe reads are not Eh on their own because that raw reading is against the probe's own reference electrode; states that getting Eh means adding the reference electrode's own potential to the measured reading
